values.AssociatedLNGNotes: A Howard Energy Partners release from December 2023 says the Spears project was built to move up to 1 Bcf/d of South Texas gas to Gulf Coast LNG facilities. The Energy Information Administration lists LNG among the demand it serves.

verifications.note: Says the Spears project, a 62-mile 36-inch pipeline, carries up to 1 Bcf/d to growing Gulf Coast LNG facilities and was built in response to LNG market demand.
Spears Expansion Project entry lists demand served as Electric, Industrial, LNG.

records.researcher_notes: No single terminal is named. Sources say Gulf Coast LNG facilities in general, so the terminal cell stays blank.

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: A Williams fact sheet from March 2026 says Driftwood Line 200 will connect Woodside's Louisiana LNG export facility to Transco and other pipelines. The Energy Information Administration lists LNG as the demand served.

verifications.note: Fact sheet says Driftwood Line 200 connects Woodside's Louisiana LNG export facility to major regional pipelines.
Driftwood Line 200 and 300 Project Phase 1 entry lists demand served as LNG and describes the Woodside Louisiana LNG feed-gas corridor.

records.researcher_notes: The sheet had Driftwood LNG Terminal. That is the same terminal, which GEM's LNG terminal tracker now names Woodside Louisiana LNG Terminal after Woodside bought Tellurian, so the tracker's name is used.

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: The Energy Information Administration lists LNG as the demand served by Line 300 and ties the Line 200 and 300 system to the Woodside Louisiana LNG feed-gas corridor. Woodside presents Line 200 and Line 300 on its Louisiana LNG project pipeline page.

verifications.note: Phase 2 entry for the remainder of Line 300 lists demand served as LNG.
Woodside Louisiana LNG project page describes Line 200 and Line 300 and the LNG plants near Lake Charles they supply.

records.researcher_notes: The Williams fact sheet covers Line 200 only, so it is not cited here. The tie for Line 300 rests on the Energy Information Administration entry and Woodside's project page.

ledger.note: Donlin Gold signed to buy gas from the Alaska LNG pipeline, but that is a fuel supply for the mine. This 315-mile line from Cook Inlet serves the mine and is not tied to LNG exports by any source found.
Howard Energy Partners says the Spears project carries gas to Gulf Coast LNG facilities. No single terminal is named.
The Dude Lateral serves a proposed Kinetik gas processing plant in New Mexico. The Federal Register notice and the Energy Information Administration entry do not mention LNG.

The existing Double E line takes Delaware Basin gas to Waha. Sources for the line itself name no LNG tie. The Energy Information Administration lists LNG among demand for the separate compression expansion, which has no row in this chunk.
This is the cancelled original oil pipeline proposal from Oklahoma to New Mexico. It has no LNG tie.
The Red Hills Lateral was a cancelled Permian supply lateral. The filings only describe meter station connections and name no LNG tie.
A Williams fact sheet confirms Line 200 connects to Woodside's Louisiana LNG export facility. The existing terminal name is kept and the Woodside name is added.
The Energy Information Administration lists LNG as the demand served by Line 300, and Woodside's project page covers the line.
